test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A town had a population of 50,000 in 1988. In one year, by 1989, it increased by 25%. Next year, in 1990, it decreased by 30%. The next year, in 1991, there was an increase of 40%. What is the population at the end of 1991?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Multiplying Factor** method for successive changes.

Net Multiplier = (1 + 25/100) × (1 − 30/100) × (1 + 40/100)

Net Multiplier = 1.25 × 0.7 × 1.4 = 1.225

Final Population = 50,000 × 1.225 = 61,250

**∴ The correct answer is 61,250.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial population in **1988** = 50,000. Changes: +25% in **1989**, −30% in **1990**, and +40% in **1991**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f60371a3468ac9650f1c4ab0f6fc2593ef3953c361fe18cbd5feed822c7aef1.png] 

⇒ Population in **1989** = 50,000 × (125/100) = 62,500

⇒ Population in **1990** = 62,500 × (70/100) = 43,750

⇒ Population at the end of **1991** = 43,750 × (140/100)

⇒ Final Population = 43,750 × 1.4 = 61,250

**∴ The correct answer is 61,250.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net change is (a + b + ab/100)%. For multiple changes, use the multiplier method.

Population Growth Formula

Final value = Initial value × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100) ... where r is the rate of increase (+) or decrease (−).

Fraction Equivalents

Converting percentages to fractions simplifies calculations: 25% = 1/4 (factor 5/4), 30% = 3/10 (factor 7/10), 40% = 2/5 (factor 7/5).</p
